message.content:
I don’t have access to live sensor feeds, so I can’t give you an exact reading at this very moment.  
For up‑to‑date information on Los Angeles’ air quality you can check one (or more) of the following:

| Source | What it offers |
|--------|----------------|
| **AirNow** – U.S. EPA’s official site | Real‑time PM₂.₅/PM₁₀, Ozone, NO₂ levels plus forecasted “Good / Moderate / Unhealthy” categories. |
| **AQICN.org** – World Air Quality Index project | Global map with hourly updates, historical trends, and health advisories. |
| **Los Angeles County Department of Public Health** | Local alerts, smog warnings, and public‑health guidance. |
| **Weather apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Often include an “air quality index” widget based on local monitoring stations. |

If you’re looking for something specific—like how long today’s smog will last, or whether outdoor exercise is safe—you’ll find those details under each source’s “Health Advisory” section.

Let me know if you'd like help interpreting the numbers once you've checked them!
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in LA. We cannot provide real-time data; we should explain limitation and suggest resources like AirNow or AQICN. No tool needed.
